ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening against: (i) the New Zealand consolidated sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) under the United Nations Act 1946 and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the US OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN lists, adopted as international best practice by New Zealand reporting entities; and (iv) the UK HMT sanctions list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011. Verification requires tracing the ownership and control chain to all natural persons at or above the 25% threshold, together with source-of-funds and source-of-wealth assessment for any PEP exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office — New Zealand Companies Register (online portal: app.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be filed in Latin (Roman) script in English or Te Reo Māori; only alphabetic characters, numbers and specified punctuation (spaces, &, ', ., -, ()) are accepted; the legal suffix 'Limited' (or 'Tapui') is mandatory for every limited-liability company; names must not contravene s 23 of the Companies Act 1993 (misleading, offensive, or inconsistent with the public interest).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant may: (1) file a fresh application with amended distinguishing tokens and cite the statutory grounds under ss 22–23 of the Companies Act 1993; (2) submit a written request for administrative reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the rejection notice, attaching legal submissions and evidence of prior use or goodwill; (3) where the Registrar maintains the objection, institute judicial-review proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. An approved name reservation that is not yet converted into an incorporation may be extended upon payment of the prescribed extension fee while the incorporation filing remains pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a non-resident international company provided that a physical street address in New Zealand (not a PO Box) is maintained as the registered office for service of documents under s 224 of the Companies Act 1993; commercial virtual-office arrangements are acceptable where the service provider holds a lawful physical New Zealand address, a resident natural person accepts service of process, and the agent's signed consent is lodged with the Companies Office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated 5–10% annual probability for this low-risk digital services company; primarily triggered by AML/CFT supervisor (Department of Internal Affairs) thematic reviews or Inland Revenue compliance audits; routine unannounced premises inspection by the Companies Registrar is not standard practice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand): sections 10–16 (application for registration and Registrar powers), section 20 and Schedule 1 (constitution of company), sections 21–24 (name requirements), sections 30–35 (issue of shares and share capital), sections 40–42 (share certificates and register of members), section 110 (registered office), sections 151–156 (appointment of directors and officers), section 244 (annual return obligations); supplemented by the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016 and the Financial Markets Supervisory Act 2013 in respect of corporate service provider oversight.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit within the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), acting through the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 6 – Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Act 1993), filed electronically through the Companies Register and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) online portal, together with the Company Constitution and executed director and shareholder consents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required by the Companies Act 1993. An International Company formed as a company limited by shares may be incorporated with an issued capital of one ordinary share at NZD 1.00 or any nominal value stated in the constitution. No bank escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up capital verification is mandated by the Registrar of Companies for this entity class.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
IN THE MATTER OF the Companies Act 1993 AND IN THE MATTER OF [Company Name] Limited (the 'Company'), an International Company established to conduct global app store optimization, multilingual organic search, and localization agency services:

UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS

RESOLVED:

1. Share Capital Subscription: That the Company do hereby issue and allot one (1) ordinary share of NZD 1.00 nominal value, or such fully paid-up consideration as recorded in the register of members, to the initial subscriber shareholder, free of any statutory escrow or capital deposit condition, and that the directors be and are hereby authorized to receive the agreed subscription consideration, issue share certificates, and record the allotment in the register of members.

2. Adoption of Constitution and Registered Office: That the Constitution of the Company, lodged with the Registrar pursuant to section 20 of the Companies Act 1993, be and is hereby adopted, and that the registered office of the Company in New Zealand, as required by section 110 of the Companies Act 1993, be established at [Registered Office Address, New Zealand], with the address for service designated therein and the records of the Company kept at that office.

3. Appointment of Officers: That the following persons be and are hereby appointed as officers of the Company for the ensuing year and until successors are duly appointed: (a) [Director Name] as sole or managing director, satisfying the statutory requirement that at least one director be resident in New Zealand or resident in Australia and a director of a New Zealand-incorporated company; (b) [Secretary Name], if appointed, as company secretary with custodianship of the statutory registers; and (c) [Authorized Signatory Name] as the authorized signatory for payment-rail operations, with full authority to open, operate, and close corporate accounts with Wise B2B and Payoneer, to execute institutional KYC/AML onboarding documentation, and to appoint sub-delegates for compliance administration.

4. Tax Election and Foreign-Sourced Income Status: That the directors be and are hereby authorized to register the Company with Inland Revenue for an IRD number, to elect the Company's tax classification as a non-resident-incorporated company earning foreign-sourced income, and to establish its position within the tax-exempt-zone framework of the Income Tax Act 2007 (New Zealand), such that no New Zealand income tax liability will arise on non-New-Zealand-sourced agency income absent a New Zealand taxable presence or permanent establishment.

5. General Authority: That the officers be and are hereby jointly and severally irrevocably authorized to execute, notarize, apostille, and lodge all documents, including banking, payment-rail, and overseas corporate filings, as may be required to give full force and effect to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register Online and NZBN Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name '[Company Name] Limited' (or its Maori equivalent 'Tauhoko') is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity or reserved name. Reserve the name online for NZD 10.50, or alternatively include the name request within the subsequent Form 6 application. Verify compliance with section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 regarding undesirable names and with the Companies (Clarification of Company Names) Act 2014. Obtain the written consent of any third party whose name, trademark, or goodwill may be affected by the proposed name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and legal suffix
Companies Register name availability search report
Written consent from third party where the name includes restricted words, existing marks, or a personal name
Name reservation confirmation receipt (if reserved separately)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the name as undesirable, confusingly similar, or infringing, submit an amended name reservation with distinctive geographic, descriptive, or coined elements within four business days, or file a formal response under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. If a third-party objection is received, provide evidence of prior use, acquired distinctiveness, or common-law rights; failing that, select and reserve a new name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Governance Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE, in conjunction with appointed registered legal counsel or corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and settle the Company Constitution in accordance with section 20 and Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993, including provisions on share classes, director powers and residency, quorum, conflict-of-interest protocols, director and officer indemnity, and a declaration that the Company is an International Company conducting offshore-facing digital agency services. Prepare executed written consents of each director, any company secretary, and each subscriber shareholder, together with a director compliance certificate confirming that the Company will carry on only lawful activities, that each director is not disqualified under sections 151–153 of the Act, and that the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Draft Company Constitution
Consent to act as director
Consent to act as company secretary (if applicable)
Shareholder subscriber statement and share subscription agreement
Director compliance certificate
Registered office consent and address-for-service notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office returns the governance documentation for formal deficiency, amend the constitution or consents to cure each noted defect and resubmit within the stated response window. Where a director is found disqualifiable under the Act, replace the affected director and file a revised consent, or obtain relief from the High Court under section 153 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Form 6 – Application for Registration of a Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically lodge Form 6 with the Registrar of Companies through the Companies Register online portal, providing: the proposed company name; the adopted constitution; the physical registered office address in New Zealand; the address for service; full legal names, addresses, and dates of birth of all directors and shareholders; the share structure; and electronic contact details. Each director and shareholder must complete RealMe identity verification, either in person with a justice of the peace or via an approved digital identity service. Pay the online incorporation fee of NZD 61.10 by credit card; the Registrar examines the application under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993 and issues a certificate of incorporation under section 15 upon satisfaction of all statutory requirements.
required_dossiers: Form 6 – Application for Registration of a Company (electronic filing)
Company Constitution attached to the application
Written consent to act of each director
Written consent to act of each subscriber shareholder
RealMe-verified identity documents for each director and shareholder (passport or national ID and proof of residential address)
Registered office consent from the occupier of the New Zealand premises
Payment receipt for the official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an information deficiency notice under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993, respond within the prescribed period, normally 14 to 20 working days, supplying corrected data or additional evidence. If the application is rejected, rectify the stated grounds and re-lodge a fresh application; the initial filing fee is generally retained. In the event of an alleged wrongful refusal, seek internal review by the Registrar and thereafter judicial review through the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon the Registrar's satisfaction as to statutory compliance, the Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically, stating the company number and the date and time of incorporation, and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is automatically allocated. Verify the Company Extract (Company Details Report) on the Companies Register for exact correctness of the company name, company number, registered office, directors, shareholders, and shareholding. Under section 16 of the Companies Act 1993 the Company comes into existence as a body corporate on the date and time stated in the certificate, with full legal capacity and limited liability.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (downloadable electronic copy)
NZBN confirmation notice
Company Extract / Company Details Report
Companies Register entry confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or Company Extract contains any error, apply to the Registrar for rectification of the register under section 145 of the Companies Act 1993, attaching evidence of the correct particulars. The Registrar may issue an amended certificate or corrected extract administratively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and Tax-Exempt-Zone Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (IRD), New Zealand, through the NZBN online account and MyIR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN, register the Company with Inland Revenue to obtain an IRD number. Submit tax registration particulars including, inter alia, the legal entity name, company number, principal business activity industry classification (ISIC 7310 / Advertising Agencies and related New Zealand Business Industry Classification code), and New Zealand bank account or payment-rail references. Elect the applicable income tax classification under the Income Tax Act 2007, confirming that the International Company will claim the foreign-sourced income exemption where central management and control are exercised outside New Zealand, thereby situating the entity within the tax-exempt-zone model for offshore agency income. Apply for GST registration only if the Company carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand; an International Company supplying services wholly to offshore clients may remain unregistered for GST while retaining its IRD number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN registration confirmation
Company Constitution
Director and shareholder identity verification forms for Inland Revenue
Tax classification / residency questionnaire
Principal business activity classification statement (ISIC 7310)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the non-resident classification or the foreign-sourced income exemption, provide a detailed operational profile, executed offshore client contracts, and board minutes demonstrating central management and control outside New Zealand. If compulsory GST registration is imposed incorrectly, respond by filing an exemption statement or voluntary deregistration where the supply is exclusively non-New-Zealand and outside the scope of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings and Payment-Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (annual return obligations), Inland Revenue, and the institutional compliance departments of Wise B2B and Payoneer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record the First Board Resolution in the Company minute book and file the governance documents in the registered office records. Notify the Companies Office of any changes to directors, secretary, registered office, or address for service using the applicable Companies Office notification forms. Open corporate accounts with Wise B2B and Payoneer by submitting the certified Certificate of Incorporation, Constitution, First Board Resolution, current Company Extract, director identification, proof of residential address, and a beneficial ownership declaration; complete each institution's KYC/AML onboarding reflecting the Low_Risk_Standard App Growth Agency commercial model. Thereafter maintain the annual return obligation under section 244 of the Companies Act 1993 (annual return filing fee NZD 34.00) and maintain the Company's statutory records at the New Zealand registered office.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificate of Incorporation
Company Constitution
First Board Resolution (original or certified copy)
Company Extract dated within 30 days
Passport or government-issued ID of each director and beneficial owner
Proof of residential address for AML/KYC purposes
Beneficial ownership register / PSC register (if applicable)
Wise B2B corporate application form and service agreement
Payoneer corporate application form and service agreement
Annual return status confirmation and fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Wise B2B or Payoneer raises AML/KYC queries, respond through the institution's compliance officer with notarized or apostilled corporate documents, the executed offshore service contract, and a source-of-funds declaration. If the Companies Office issues an annual-return reminder or penalty assessment, file the return and pay the late renewal fee within the notice period or apply for remission on reasonable-cause grounds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment) — general occupational health and safety oversight authority; no sectoral industrial licensing board applies to digital marketing, app store optimization, or localization agency services under ISIC 7310.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — New Zealand statute does not mandate an operating, industrial, or manufacturing permit for the provision of app store optimization, multilingual organic search, and localization agency services (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810). The entity is a purely digital service provider and does not conduct regulated manufacturing, food, pharmaceutical, or export-controlled activity; accordingly, no operational license is applied for or held.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, acting under the Resource Management Act 1991, the Environmental Protection Authority Act 2011, and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a digital services operation involving no physical installation, plant construction, manufacturing facility, or emissions-generating asset. No Environmental Impact Assessment, resource consent under sections 9 and 15 of the Resource Management Act 1991, or activity-specific environmental permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable: the operation generates no point-source wastewater discharge, no volatile organic compound emissions, and no industrial waste streams. The leased office premises must nonetheless comply with local territorial authority trade-waste and recycling bylaws; electronic waste (e-waste) from IT equipment must be handled through accredited e-waste recyclers under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; and any hazardous substances used in the office require an inventory and labelling compliance record under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance: The leased registered office must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness issued by the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004, including a Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) approved evacuation scheme where the premises exceed prescribed occupancy thresholds, together with annual fire-safety system inspection certificates. Structural Clearance: A structural load compliance inspection report or building certificate confirming the premises are fit for general office use must be retained. Occupational Clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, comprising a written workplace health and safety policy, hazard identification register, first-aid provisions, worker participation system, and emergency response protocols; for remote or home-based workers, a completed home-workspace self-assessment must be archived.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; taxpayer digital portal: myIR (Secure Online Services via www.ird.govt.nz); business identity registry: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step-by-step procedure for a foreign-owned International Company (IC) to obtain a New Zealand IRD number and GST registration: (1) Register the company with the New Zealand Companies Office and obtain an NZBN; (2) Apply for an IRD number through the non-resident company application process (Form IR742 or myIR online application), providing certificate of incorporation, registered office details, director particulars, and, if required, a New Zealand agent address; (3) Register for GST via myIR or Form IR356, electing a filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly) and declaring the date the taxable activity commenced; (4) Where the IC is a non-resident supplier of remote or digital services to New Zealand consumers, use the dedicated non-resident GST registration pathway under section 54B of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (5) Receive the 8-9 digit IRD number and confirmation notice; the IRD number serves as the single statutory tax identification number for income tax, GST, PAYE, and FBT (New Zealand does not maintain a separate VAT ID).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — non-resident territorial scope: the International Company is subject to New Zealand income tax only on New Zealand-source income (sections BD 1 and YA 1, Income Tax Act 2007); foreign-sourced revenue derived from App Store Optimization (ASO), multilingual SEO, and localization services is outside the New Zealand tax net absent a New Zealand permanent establishment (PE); no entity-level taxation applies to offshore income; any deemed New Zealand-source income is taxed on a net basis at the 28% corporate rate, with no New Zealand capital gains tax on offshore assets.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not apply a US-style check-the-box classification regime; statutory elections available to a foreign-owned International Company include: (a) GST grouping election under section 55 of the GST Act 1985, allowing eligible companies to be treated as a single GST group; (b) consolidated group election under subpart FM of the Income Tax Act 2007, permitting wholly-owned resident group companies to file as one tax entity; (c) hybrid mismatch elections under the Taxation (Neutralising Arising Mismatches) Act 2018, including deemed deduction and offset elections to neutralize hybrid financial instrument outcomes; (d) group loss offset election under subpart IC of the Income Tax Act 2007, enabling intra-group loss transfers; (e) branch-equivalent election under the controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution rules in subpart EX of the Income Tax Act 2007, electing to tax CFC income on a branch-equivalent basis; (f) non-resident GST registration election under section 54B of the GST Act 1985, simplifying registration for non-resident suppliers of remote digital services. No pass-through or entity-level check-the-box elections exist in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) — New Zealand's value-added consumption tax administered by Inland Revenue under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; functionally equivalent to VAT or GST regimes in other jurisdictions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (section 51, Goods and Services Tax Act 1985); non-resident suppliers of remote services, including digital marketing, ASO, SEO, and localization services, must register for GST once the aggregate value of supplies to New Zealand consumers exceeds NZD 60,000; voluntary registration is permitted under section 51(3) for persons carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand, including non-residents supplying goods from outside New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime applies in New Zealand. Taxpayers may issue standard electronic invoices; voluntary PEPPOL-BIS 3.0 e-invoicing interoperability is supported through the New Zealand E-Invoice network for B2B transactions, but no transactional API clearance obligation exists. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR, and IRD APIs permit XML-based GST return submission and status queries. Taxpayers must retain complete electronic and physical records sufficient to substantiate zero-rated exports; inadequate record-keeping attracts the general anti-avoidance and penalty provisions of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Services, including ASO, SEO, and localization services, supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply are zero-rated under section 11A(1)(k) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, provided the services are not physically performed in New Zealand; remote or digital services supplied to non-resident businesses on a B2B basis are zero-rated under section 11A(1)(m); goods are zero-rated under section 11 where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of supply and holds documentary evidence of export. The supplier must verify the non-resident status of the recipient and maintain records sufficient to demonstrate the offshore nexus; where zero-rating is claimed incorrectly, output tax at 15% is payable together with consequential penalties and interest.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or New Zealand Customs electronic cargo movement record evidencing physical export of goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing transport of goods out of New Zealand
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in NZD or foreign currency
Executed service agreement, Statement of Work, and delivery evidence substantiating the supply of zero-rated remote services
Recipient non-residency declaration, Tax Residence Certificate, or zero-rated export invoice containing the required statutory particulars
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims with heightened scrutiny of digital service exporters, applying a substance-over-form analysis to determine whether services were physically performed in New Zealand or supplied to a genuine non-resident. Incorrect zero-rating results in retrospective reassessment and clawback of the full 15% GST, plus use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties under Part 4A of the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for an abusive tax position. Fraudulent zero-rating or false export documentation constitutes tax evasion under section 143A and knowingly providing false information under section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying criminal conviction, substantial fines, and imprisonment for individuals; the standard 4-year reassessment limitation period is extended to 8 years in cases of fraud or non-disclosure, permitting retrospective clawback across additional tax periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ / Te Pūtea Matua) under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021; AML/CFT supervisory powers are also shared with the Financial Markets Authority and the Department of Internal Affairs, but RBNZ is the central bank for FX and prudential policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: NZD is freely convertible. New Zealand maintains no exchange-control law that restricts current-account or capital-account transactions, foreign-currency account balances, or settlement of bona fide trade invoices. Profit distribution, dividends, loan repayments, interest, royalties, and liquidation proceeds may be remitted offshore upon satisfaction of New Zealand tax withholding and reporting requirements (NRWT/RLWT) but without RBNZ approval. The only material approvals are the Overseas Investment Act 2005 screening rules for foreign acquisitions of sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets above the relevant thresholds; a cross-border digital marketing/localization agency transacting operational share capital and service invoices is not within those screening categories unless it is acquiring sensitive New Zealand assets or a substantial New Zealand business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand does not impose mandatory surrender, repatriation, conversion, or declaration deadlines for export proceeds. An exporter of app-store optimization and multilingual organic search services can lawfully invoice in USD, EUR, or any agreed currency, retain collections in a New Zealand foreign-currency account, and convert at a time of its choosing. Banks will apply standard CDD/AML checks and record the international transaction for statistical BOP reporting, but no RBNZ approval or conversion ratio applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for day-to-day low-value disbursements and sub-contractor payments; Medium as a full treasury replacement. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise (Wise B2B) and Payoneer may settle low-value international invoices rapidly and integrate into the intended payment rails. Legal constraints: they are not New Zealand registered banks or licensed deposit-takers; they hold client money under safeguarding/trust arrangements rather than accepting deposits, must comply with the AML/CFT Act 2009 and Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 if operating into New Zealand, and may impose stricter UBO/substance checks on tax-exempt offshore International Companies. They should be used only for small/medium operational flows; high-value settlements, LC transactions, and strategic FX hedging should be routed through a Tier 1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statute or RBNZ rule mandates that directors appear physically at a New Zealand branch to open an account. Remote onboarding is permitted where the bank can complete customer due diligence using reliable independent digital identity verification or certified documentation. In practice, Tier 1 banks will require a video interview or notarised/certified identity documents from non-resident directors, plus a board resolution and corporate file; a director located abroad can usually sign electronically and have documents apostilled in their home jurisdiction. A physical face-to-face meeting is generally required only when the bank assesses the entity as high risk, or when the corporate structure cannot provide verifiable beneficial-ownership/source-of-funds information.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company (IC) applying for a New Zealand bank account with no New Zealand tax presence or filed returns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, constitution/memorandum, register of directors and shareholders, tax-residence certificate from the home jurisdiction, legal analysis explaining the IC's tax-exempt status and why no NZ tax return is due, plus evidence of economic substance (office lease, staffing, business plan, service contracts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and remote shareholders causing beneficial-ownership opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copies, recent utility bills or bank statements proving residential addresses, a full register of ultimate beneficial owners with a shareholding/control table, a board resolution appointing the bank signatories, and any trust or foundation deed if a trust sits above the IC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected or volatile inbound flows: large capital injections, high-value app-growth invoices, or rapid round-tripping to sub-contractors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client contracts, itemised invoices with scope-of-work, payment histories, management accounts, bank statements from the originating account, and for capital injections an equity subscription agreement and board minutes evidencing the share issue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital marketing/app-growth sector with potential exposure to gambling, crypto, or regulated app verticals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An AML-compliant client intake policy, current client due-diligence files with beneficial-owner details and sanctions screening, a no-gambling/no-crypto certification where applicable, and a written undertaking not to process prohibited merchant categories through the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Wise/Payoneer or non-bank rails in parallel with the bank account, triggering a fragmentation concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy describing permitted payment rails, reconciliations showing transfers between fintech balances and the bank account are transparent, and confirmation that the fintech account is owned by the same legal entity with matching KYC documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should be remitted by wire from the overseas shareholder's account to the IC's New Zealand bank account using SWIFT MT103, with the beneficiary stated as the IC and remittance information referencing 'Equity subscription / share capital contribution'. New Zealand banks do not use a prescribed national purpose-code table, but the customer must provide a commercial declaration in the bank's remittance form; a common safe description is 'Equity contribution for share subscription under Companies Act 1993'. For ordinary agency capitalization below the Overseas Investment Act screening thresholds and with no sensitive assets, no RBNZ or Government approval is required. The bank will perform CDD and may place the funds on temporary hold pending verification of the subscription agreement and source of funds; directors should pre-submit the corporate file and board resolution before the wire is dispatched. Large injections above NZD 100 million or acquisitions of sensitive New Zealand assets require separate Overseas Investment Act screening; this is generally irrelevant for a bootstrap or mid-cap digital agency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border vendor payments, contractor settlements, and profit distributions should be cleared through the SWIFT network using MT103 for outright client/vendor payments, MT202/MT202 COV for correspondent-bank transfers, and MT700/MT707 for commercial letters of credit and amendments. NZD leg settlement between local banks is cleared through RBNZ-operated ESAS/NZClear; USD, EUR, or GBP legs are settled via the bank's overseas correspondent network. For low-value disbursements to independent service providers and SEO localization freelancers, Wise B2B or Payoneer local-currency rails can be used as ancillary channels, provided the recipient's virtual account is in the IC's name and the transfer is matched to a signed work order. Large disbursements and any settlement under a commercial LC should be executed from the Tier 1 bank rather than a fintech balance to avoid rejection by counterparty banks and to maintain proper EUR/GBP/USD clearing records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in NZD vs USD, EUR, GBP, AUD and CNY (standard with Tier 1 banks; maturity usually up to 12 months, extendable to 24 months under ISDA/account terms)
Cross-currency swaps for matched funding or to hedge intercompany loan exposure
Vanilla FX options and option combos (call spreads, put spreads, cost-reversal structures) where the bank's ISDA/CSA documentation permits options

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the underlying exposure is to a deliverable-restricted currency such as CNY/INR; NZD itself is fully deliverable so NDFs are not necessary for NZD/USD hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993 ss 208-212) — confirmation of director, shareholder, registered office and beneficial ownership particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Registrar of Companies (NZ Companies Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reminder due within 20 working days after the company's Annual Return Date (the last day of the month containing the incorporation anniversary); no AR date reset available for a standard private company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar serves a Notice of Default; if the return is not filed within 20 working days after the notice, the company is automatically removed from the New Zealand register; each director in default also commits an offence under s 214(1), carrying a fine of up to NZD 40,000 (approximately USD 25,000).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (if non-exempt under Financial Reporting Act 2013 — e.g., overseas-owned or 'large' profile)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Registrar of Companies (NZ Companies Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the registered balance date; for the standard 31 March financial year this falls in early July (6 July), with extension up to 12 months after balance date if the company has a valid tax agent extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringement and late-filing levies under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (up to NZD 1,000 for non-issuers and NZD 10,000 for issuers, approximately USD 620-6,200); persistent non-supply can lead to a further Registrar strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempt / nil annual income tax return for the tax-exempt International Company (attestation of qualifying status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 7 July immediately following the 31 March standard balance date (or within 12 months of a non-standard balance date approved by IRD / tax agent extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 commence at NZD 250 (approximately USD 155) for small companies and NZD 500 (approximately USD 310) for other companies; repeated default increases the penalty to a maximum of NZD 1,000 (approximately USD 620), plus automatic late-payment interest (currently about 9.94% p.a.) and the risk of criminal 'knowingly fails' sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company exceeds 'large' thresholds (consolidated total assets above NZD 6M or annual revenue above NZD 15M), is a subsidiary of a large/overseas parent, or is an FMC reporting entity or issuer; otherwise the offshore International Company is audit-exempt unless shareholders or a group policy require an audit or review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (Tier 1) for large companies; NZ GAAP - Tier 2 (medium), Tier 3 (small simplified) or Tier 4 (minimal reporting) for smaller companies, as applicable to the entity's public accountability and size

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no public separate UBO register for private companies; the Annual Return acts as the annual beneficial-ownership confirmation by attesting current shareholder and ultimate-owner particulars. Any share transfer must be entered in the Register of Members and the shareholding change reflected in the current Annual Return; AML/CFT 'reporting entities' engaged by the company must further obtain and verify beneficial-ownership evidence at onboarding and on any material ownership change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 700 (New Zealand registered office and registered agent services for a non-resident International Company)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,500 for a statutory audit (if large); USD 1,200 - 2,500 for an independent review/attestation where audit is not compulsory

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential corporate income tax rates exist in New Zealand. The standard 28% corporate rate applies universally. Certain research and development activities may qualify for a 15% tax credit (subject to conditions), but this is not a territorial or entity-based exemption. New Zealand does not operate an 'International Company' or tax-exempt zone regime for resident companies; all resident companies are taxed on worldwide income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (subject to continuity of beneficial ownership and business continuity rules under New Zealand tax law)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR6 Company Tax Return; electronically filed via Inland Revenue's MyIR portal (myIR). Non-resident companies with New Zealand-source income may also use IR6 with appropriate disclosures.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with compulsory provisional tax payments during the year for liabilities exceeding NZD 5,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR6 must be filed by 7 July following the balance date (extended to 7 April of the following year for terminal tax payment). Non-standard balance dates require a valid Inland Revenue-approved accounting year-end; the filing deadline is generally 6 months after the balance date. Terminal tax for non-standard balance dates is due on the 15th of the month following the 6-month filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year end date and corresponding income year (e.g., 31 March 2025).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand balance date; if the non-resident company has a non-standard balance date approved by Inland Revenue, enter that date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income calculated under New Zealand tax law after all deductions, exemptions, and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only New Zealand-source taxable income and report amounts in New Zealand dollars (NZD). Apportion global income where required under tax treaties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits, R&D tax credits, foreign tax credits, and other lodged credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed only in respect of New Zealand-source income taxed abroad if a DTA applies; otherwise, claim only statutory credits specifically available to non-residents (e.g., non-resident withholding tax offsets).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax position after applying credits, provisional tax paid, and terminal tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Articulate any withholding tax already deducted from New Zealand-sourced dividends, royalties, or interest to reduce terminal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Closing balance of the company's imputation credit account for resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies without resident shareholders are not required to maintain an imputation credit account; leave nil unless a residence election or DTA impact applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR6 attracts an immediate penalty of NZD 250 (NZD 500 if IR6 remains outstanding after the initial grace period), plus automatic deductions of the same amount if still unfiled 30 days after the original penalty assessment. Late payment of tax incurs a 1% late-payment penalty on the first day overdue, followed by a 4% penalty at day 8, and a further 1% per month on the unpaid amount thereafter. Inland Revenue may also impose a shortfall penalty for inaccurate or incomplete returns (20% or 40% depending on whether the inaccuracy is substantial and/or arises from abusive tax avoidance).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company to non-resident shareholders. The rate may be reduced under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA); typically 15% under most treaties, with lower rates for certain major shareholdings (e.g., 5% under the New Zealand-Australia DTA for a 10%+ holding).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA-reduced withholding rates, the non-resident payee must provide the New Zealand-resident payer with a completed 'IRS/NRWT rate claim' declaration (form IRD 485 or equivalent DTA declaration) before the payment is made. The payee must also obtain and submit a certificate of fiscal residence (Tax Residence Certificate, TRC) from their home-country tax authority to evidence treaty entitlement. The payer applies the reduced rate at source; if a higher rate is withheld, the non-resident may claim a refund from Inland Revenue by filing an IR3NR return, attaching the TRC and a statement of income, within the relevant statutory claim period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties and interest paid by New Zealand residents to non-residents is 15%. Under DTAs, rates are typically reduced to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, provided the beneficial owner is a resident of the treaty jurisdiction. The same administrative protocol as for dividends applies: DTA declaration and TRC must be furnished to the payer before the reduced rate can be applied. For related-party interest, thin capitalisation rules may also apply to disallow excessive interest deductions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand does not prescribe a bright-line NZD threshold triggering mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. However, the Inland Revenue may require TP documentation when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 2 million per annum per related party. Large multinational groups with global revenue exceeding EUR 750 million (approximately NZD 1.3 billion) are subject to country-by-country reporting (CbCR), master file, and local file obligations if they are New Zealand tax residents or have a New Zealand presence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) akin to the Cayman Islands or BVI regime. Instead, the tax law applies a general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, plus specific 'PE' and 'sufficient substance' principles embedded in tax treaty case law. To benefit from DTA protection (e.g., reduced withholding rates), the New Zealand resident payer must ensure the payee is the legal and beneficial owner of the income and has substantive business activity in its claimed residence jurisdiction. A shell company without physical office, staff, or real commercial operations may be denied treaty benefits and be re-characterised as not treaty-eligible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to disclose New Zealand-source income; filing false IR6 returns; understating turnover; creating artificial invoicing structures to divert profits to unreported offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Maximum fine of NZD 50,000 for a company; for individuals, a fine up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. Civil shortfall penalties typically 150% of the tax shortfall attributable to evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the company's unpaid taxes under section 76 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 for GST and PAYE. For income tax, directors may be personally liable under the 'quasi-security' provisions if the company's scheme of arrangement has a purpose of avoiding tax. Courts may also pierce the corporate veil for fraudulent conduct, enabling recovery of penalties from directors and imposing travel bans and director prohibition under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a New Zealand company with no real office, personnel, or local operations, interposed solely to route dividends or royalties to a third-country resident to access treaty benefits (treaty shopping) without conducting any substantive commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the GAAR (section BG 1) to strike down the arrangement, reconstruction of the actual taxpayer, a shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the avoided tax (100% for abusive tax position), and denial of DTA relief. Fines under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 may also apply to non-compliant trust or company service providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell company may be personally assessed for the resultant tax shortfall if they knowingly created or participated in an arrangement with a dominant purpose of tax avoidance. They may face civil prohibition orders and debtor travel restrictions where the company owes outstanding tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Facilitating cross-border payments through Wise B2B or Payoneer without conducting proper customer due diligence; accepting unexplained funds, processing payments for third parties without contractual documentation, or bypassing beneficial ownership verification for a Panamanian-style entity structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, reporting entities (including payment service providers and financial advisers) must enforce a risk-based AML programme. Non-compliance may lead to civil penalty orders of up to NZD 200,000 per contravention for individuals and up to NZD 2 million for companies. Criminal fines of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment up to one year apply to wilful non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers may incur personal civil and criminal liability if they knowingly fail to implement adequate AML/CFT policies, permit suspicious transactions, or obstruct Inland Revenue or FIU investigations. Travel ban orders may be issued pending investigation of money-laundering predicates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a dividend or royalty/interest to a non-resident without withholding NRWT, or misclassifying a dividend as a non-taxable loan extension or service fee to avoid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 28 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 requires deduction of NRWT. Failure to deduct results in a withholding penalty of 10% of the full amount withheld per due date, plus late payment penalties (1% daily up to 10% maximum), and a shortfall penalty of 20% to 150%. The company remains fully liable for the gross NRWT amount plus penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused or permitted payment, or signed a false declaration that NRWT was deducted, may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid NRWT, and may face an unpaid-recovery interdiction order (travel ban) preventing departure from New Zealand until the tax is paid.
